set.approach: From the hut beside the lake, walk back around the shore to the second avalanche slide path on Mount Shadowfax, a short walk of under ten minutes. Climb the lower slopes through a talus field into the heart of the couloir. Higher up it steepens and splits into two branches; the route takes the climber's right branch. The hut itself is a couple of hours from the summer parking, longer in deep snow.
set.descent_text: The couloir tops out on a subsummit. From there, head toward the true summit and drop to the low point on the ridge between them, which gives access to the left-hand branch of the couloir system. Walk down that branch; it is easy and needs no rappels.

review.notes: Approach and no-rappel descent agree on both pages.

set.approach: Most parties are flown in and land on Rainy Knob beside the Tiedemann Glacier, because large crevasses make a landing on the glacier itself impractical. Flights happen in daylight, so the first evening goes to watching for avalanche and rockfall hazard and preparing for an early alpine start. The route then follows the Bravo Glacier, passing about midway between the east ridge of Bravo Peak and the smaller southeast rib. Crossing the rib, which closes the glacier into a cul-de-sac, is the main glacier problem; the side nearer Bravo Peak is usually safer from avalanches off Spearman Peak.
set.descent_text: The standard way down reverses the summit chimney. Rappel the chimney to the notch between the Tooth and the summit tower, then downclimb the fourth-class ramp across the Tooth. A final rappel gets you past the bergschrund at its foot. Upper rappels can snag on ice feathers and loose blocks.

set.approach: The route is the farthest left line on the north face of the summit tower as seen from Combatant Col. From a camp on the col, walk a few minutes through a debris field to the bergschrund, near 9,900 ft, and cross it as far left as you can to stay clear of the seracs. Steep ice leads from there to a snow arete.
set.descent_text: Reversing the route with extensive downclimbing is possible, but the usual way down is to rappel the summit tower, go up a brief couloir onto the northwest summit shoulder, then descend the Angel Glacier. Most of this is walking, though finding the easy line through the icefall takes some searching, and several sections lie under active seracs.

set.approach: The climb starts from Waddington-Combatant Col. It crosses the bergschrund to reach the first of three pillars on the north face of Waddington. A separate ice line, the Flavelle-Lane, lies directly to the climber's right.

review.notes: Approach only; no descent stated on the page.

set.descent_text: Descend toward climbers' left and go down the first large gully, Bruggers Gully.

review.notes: Descent only; approach not described. Route is across the gully from Newman-Foweraker.

set.approach: Hike up Brugger's Gully to the base of the route, then climb a short section of AI3 ice to reach the obvious chimney entrance. Part of Mt Arrowsmith is private land, so confirm access with the landowner before heading up.

Park at the small pullout on Highway 1 just west of the Wapta road, with room for one vehicle before the cattle gate. Walk west to the wildlife overpass and go through the fence gate on your right just before it. Climb left up the hill to a ridge, drop left into the drainage and follow it up to the climb. Plan on a couple of hours, longer with snow, and bring snowshoes.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route with a double rope, going from the top to the anchor at the top of the third pitch, then to the anchor at the top of the second pitch. Make sure both ropes reach the ledge and knot the ends. Walk down the snow slope below and make a final single-rope rappel to the base.

review.notes: Single page; counts and lengths omitted.

set.approach: Park beside the highway where a drainage crosses under it, west of the gate at the Wapta road. The base is a long uphill walk of an hour or more above the road. Check the avalanche forecast before heading up.

review.notes: Approach only; page gives no descent.

set.approach: Take the Joffre Lakes trail to the upper lake, where parties often camp below the face, then continue up the Stonecrop Glacier. An easy, broad couloir cuts the lower rock bands and ends at the foot of the ice face.
set.descent_text: Descend the ridge to the Slalok-Tzsil col, which includes a steep stretch of third-class ground. From the col, go down the moraine slopes into the Tzsil Creek valley.

review.notes: Descent from route page; camp above upper Joffre Lake from the club trip page.
